sentences.text: Let’s take the two errors one at a time.
It’s caused by the earth itself.
Magnetic north and true north aren’t in the same place.
So variation depends only on where you are.
It’s the same on every heading.
You read it from the center of the nearest compass rose on your chart.
The rose also gives the year it was measured and the annual change.
So what do you do with a rose that’s fifteen years old?
Multiply the annual change by the years, and bring it up to date.
In Florida, variation is a few degrees west, from roughly two degrees in the western Panhandle to around eight on the Atlantic coast.
And westerly variation means just what it says: magnetic north lies to the west of true north.
